title: Herodotus records a king's tomb on an island in an underground lake

tellings.quote: But he records that down in the Osiris shaft there was the tomb of a great king on an island surrounded by a lake of water.

plain: Herodotus, the ancient Greek historian, wrote of the tomb of a great king "on an island surrounded by a lake of water" deep underground, and the researcher Luke Caverns ties that account to the Osiris shaft, a deep shaft cut into the ground at Giza, near the pyramids. Caverns tells Michels this as his own reading, without naming a translation, and also mentions the Egyptian archaeologist Zahi Hawass in connection with the shaft. Herodotus's words reach us here only through Caverns, and whether the tomb Herodotus described is the Osiris shaft is Caverns's reading, which the passage as he gives it neither confirms nor rules out.
